title: Meet NIVA: The nuclear industry’s own AI tool
summary: Built on decades of technical, regulatory, and operational experience, the Nuclear Industry Virtual Assistant (NIVA) is out of beta testing and in use at nuclear power plants across North America. NIVA debuted in August, featuring plain-language generative AI functions that would be familiar to people who have come to rely on AI chat tools. But NIVA’s tools, including a “knowledge assistant” and an “operating experience assistant,” are industry-specific and designed to help utilities accelerate licensing and maintenance. NIVA can make both historical lessons learned and the latest regulatory guides more accessible. It can also help newcomers to the nuclear workforce quickly learn what they need to know. What do people in the nuclear industry need to know about NIVA? It begins with how NIVA was conceived as a collaborative effort by three organizations: the Electric Power Research Institute, the Institute of Nuclear Power Operations, and the Nuclear Energy Institute. Nuclear News went to project leaders to learn more.

title: Extension for RAI responses delays Project Ike review
summary: In a decision that potentially has added two months to its projected review timeline, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission has given Orano Enrichment more time to respond to the commission’s requests for additional information regarding the Project Ike Enrichment Facility. The NRC began an accelerated technical review of Orano’s license application for the Oak Ridge, Tenn., facility in May of this year. In its May 21 letter announcing its acceptance of Orano’s application, the NRC stated that it planned to complete the expedited review by April 30, 2027.

title: Firm developing Portsmouth site data center posts $7B loss
summary: Japanese investment firm SoftBank Group, whose subsidiary SB Energy is developing what the Department of Energy calls “the world’s largest artificial intelligence data center” at the Portsmouth, Ohio, nuclear cleanup site, has posted a net quarterly loss of approximately $7 billion. The PORTS Technology Campus (also known as the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus), which the Department of Energy’s Office of Environmental Management announced in March, is slated to be home to a 10-GW AI data center developed through a partnership between SB Energy and OpenAI, with Nvidia providing computing infrastructure for the facility. According to the November 10 episode of DOE-EM’s EnergyCast podcast, the campus also will host the largest energy generation project in the United States. SB Energy has pledged to build 10 GW of new power generation at the site to support the data center, including 9.2 GW of power from natural gas–powered turbines.

title: OPG Begins ‘Comprehensive Assessment’ As Canada SMR Project Faces Delays And Budget Overruns
summary: The first of four BWRX-300 small modular reactors (SMRs) under construction at the Darlington nuclear site in Canada will not be on schedule or to budget, Ontario Power Generation (OPG) has said. OPG said in its 2026 third quarter financial results that it had previously noted that the Darlington New Nuclear Project (DNNP) is subject to “inherent risks and uncertainties that could affect project cost and schedule”.
